settings.name: MFASS splice-disrupting variant detection, full labelled cohort, average precision
settings.definition: All MFASS mutant SNVs with a v2 exon-inclusion-change measurement (27,733 variants, 1,050 splice-disrupting at an inclusion drop of at least 0.50, 3.79%). Each sequence-based predictor scores the variant in hg38 genomic context, tissue-agnostically, with no training on MFASS and no held-out split. Scored by average precision (and AUROC) over the whole cohort.

protocols.why: Protocol attributes state the cohort (27,733 SNVs, 1,050 SDVs), the 0.50 inclusion threshold, hg38 genomic context and average precision over the whole cohort.
protocols.differences: Preprint. SpliceAI variants outside annotated genes set to 0; SPANR scores 27,663 variants; MMSplice on a reconstructed context. AUROC is also reported for every tool.

protocols.why: Same assay (MFASS) and same label type: auPRC for the splice-disrupting label defined by the MFASS exon-inclusion threshold.
protocols.differences: The file does not give the variant count, the inclusion threshold value or the split: the dataset is an 'evaluated data subset', the record cites the AlphaGenome chromosome-split section, and the metric qualifier is 'all tissues pooled'. Its reference level (all-tissues auPRC 0.02) differs from Znabu's 3.79% positive rate, which suggests a different label set or prevalence. auPRC versus average precision can also differ slightly by estimator. Not comparable number for number.

settings.name: Riepe et al. ABCA4 and MYBPC3 minigene-tested variants, binary splice-alteration classification, sensitivity and specificity
settings.definition: 213 patient variants in ABCA4 (deep intronic and noncanonical splice site) and MYBPC3 (noncanonical splice site) whose splicing effect was measured in mini- or midigene assays in HEK293T cells. Each tool's score is thresholded (tuned on the same data) and scored by sensitivity and specificity against the assay label, pooled over all 213 variants.

protocols.why: Fortier Table 2 names the Riepe et al. functional splice assay variants, 213 variants in ABCA4 and MYBPC3, scored by sensitivity and specificity at a threshold optimised for accuracy.
protocols.differences: Thresholds optimised per gene and algorithm on the same data (upper bound). Fractions.

protocols.why: Riepe et al. 2021 own benchmark tables on the same mini- and midigene-tested variants; the TP, FN, TN and FP counts of the three subsets sum to 213, matching Fortier's set size.
protocols.differences: ABCA4 deep-intronic subset only (81 variants by confusion counts, 26% positive). Per-data-set cutoff, values printed as percent. A subset of the pooled set, so values are not comparable to Fortier's pooled numbers; Riepe's cutoffs are per subset, Fortier's per gene.

settings.name: Nucleotide Transformer benchmark splice acceptor classification, fine-tuned, MCC
settings.definition: Sequence-level classification on the Nucleotide Transformer benchmark splice-site dataset (acceptor). The model is fine-tuned (or trained) on the dataset's training data and scored on held-out data by Matthews correlation coefficient; NT benchmark reports the median over 10 cross-validation folds.

protocols.why: Part of the NT benchmark (18 tasks); dataset 'NT benchmark Splice acceptor'; MCC, median of 10 CV folds, parameter-efficient fine-tuning.
protocols.differences: Developer benchmark: NT authors ran every model. BPNet and random-init rows are trained from scratch.

protocols.why: Same NT benchmark dataset and MCC metric.
protocols.differences: Frozen-embedding probing, not fine-tuning, so the model input and adaptation differ; numbers are not comparable to the fine-tuned rows.

protocols.why: Dataset named 'Nucleotide Transformer benchmark splice-site dataset, acceptors'; same classification target.

notes: No formal disagreements: no setting has two sources at 'same' or 'near' that score the same model. Three leads for a human. (1) MFASS: Pangolin auPRC 0.542 in the AlphaGenome paper (alphagenome-2026-result-8cf25c8390471f0c) versus average precision 0.421 in Znabu et al. on the full 27,733-variant cohort (splicing-follow-up-20261009-result-znabu2026-pangolin-ap). The AlphaGenome subset, threshold and split are not in the file and its reference level (0.02) differs from Znabu's 3.79% prevalence, so the gap may be a different variant set; worth checking whether both use the same MFASS release and label threshold. (2) Riepe set: summing Riepe et al. 2021 confusion counts for SpliceAI 1.3.1 over the three subsets gives pooled sensitivity 91/119 = 0.765 and specificity 82/94 = 0.872 (derived, no result id), against Fortier et al. SpliceAI 0.790 and 0.883 on the same 213 variants (rna-splicing-20261011-fortier2026-result-riepe-spliceai-recall, -specificity). The small gap is consistent with Fortier tuning one threshold per gene rather than per subset. (3) NT splice datasets: You et al. and the NT paper use the same named datasets but share no metric (accuracy versus MCC) or evaluation scheme (single split, 3 seeds versus 10-fold CV median); both rank NT above DNABERT-2 on all three sets, so there is no ordering conflict to report. Existing tasks: catalog-task-mfass-splice and catalog-task-rna-splice-sites have empty descriptions, so neither was linked; beacon-task-spl has no protocol in this cluster. Model ids lump checkpoints: discovery-model-nucleotide-transformer covers 14 NT variants, regulatory-variant-20261009-model-gena-lm covers base and large, regulatory-variant-20261009-model-hyenadna covers 1KB and 32KB. Riepe et al. 2021 map Spidex to splicing-follow-up-20261009-method-spanr. Riepe 2021 values are in percent, Fortier in fractions. The cluster is mostly single-paper evaluations: of 17 distinct sources, only MFASS, the Riepe set, the NT splice datasets and GUE are reused across papers.
